transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Samir from Redwood, AE on the deal. Claire, our SE, is here as well. Quick sound check?
[00:10] Claire: Yep, all good. Thanks Samir. Hi Rajiv, Laura, Marcus.
[00:15] Rajiv: Hi, thanks. We only have 45 minutes so we'll try to go through the SIG sections that are blockers for procurement.
[00:23] Samir: Totally, we'll hit the high priority items first — SOC 2, SSO/RBAC, audit logs, data residency and encryption/KMS. We'll also note where you can accept our standard answers versus where you might require evidence.
[00:34] Laura: That sounds good. Procurement mainly wants to see SOC 2 and some explicit custody details for keys.
[00:39] Claire: Great, we'll start with SOC 2. Redwood is SOC 2 Type II, our latest report is from Q1 2026. For SIG you'll see we map controls to evidence like the SOC report, policy docs, and internal control matrices.
[00:50] Marcus: When you say "evidence" — are those uploaded somewhere, or do you share them per request? We have to track document access.
[00:57] Samir: We normally provide a redacted SOC 2 report and a link to our compliance pack. It's shared via a secure link; access is logged. If you need a NDA for the full artefacts we can do that too.
[01:10] Rajiv: Ok. Also for ISO — do you have an ISO 27001 cert or similar?
[01:14] Claire: We do not currently hold ISO 27001 at the company level; we are SOC 2 Type II and we follow ISO-aligned controls in our policy set. We can provide our policy excerpts and mapping to SIG questions.
[01:25] Rajiv: Understood. Next — SSO/SAML and RBAC. Can you walk through how Redwood handles user provisioning and role mapping?
[01:33] Claire: Sure. Redwood supports SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM provisioning for users and groups. Roles are mapped from the IdP groups to our RBAC roles; we support custom role mappings. For private deployments we can also integrate with your LDAP/AD via SAML/SCIM.
[01:48] Marcus: Is SCIM automated or just a manual sync? We prefer automated provisioning for least privilege.
[01:53] Claire: SCIM is automated, push-based. We can sync groups and deprovision users on the IdP side. For hosted customers we provide sample mappings and metadata. I'll share an example SAML metadata XML and SCIM schema.
[02:05] Samir: Action item: Claire will upload the SSO guide and metadata example to the SIG doc.
[02:11] Laura: Great. On audit logs — what do you capture and how long are they retained? We need logs for 12 months at least and the ability to export for e-discovery.
[02:20] Claire: By default our hosted logs retain 90 days in the console. For Dedicated and Private customers we offer configurable retention — we can retain 12 months or longer depending on the plan. Logs include request-level metadata, actor, timestamp, model and route, and redacted payloads by default unless you opt into full retention.
[02:40] Marcus: Redacted payloads — can we get unredacted logs under contract?
[02:44] Samir: We can, but that would require specific agreements around data handling and scope. For financial institutions we usually recommend Dedicated or Private with customer-managed KMS so keys never leave their control.
[02:56] Rajiv: That leads to KMS question — do you support customer-managed keys and what KMS providers?
[03:02] Claire: Yes, we support CMK for Dedicated and Private. We currently support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and vault-based HSM integrations. Keys can be in the customer account for Private deployments. For Hosted API we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys, but we also have a bring-your-own-key option for enterprise customers via a connector.
[03:22] Marcus: If keys are in our account, does Redwood ever hold plaintext?
[03:26] Claire: No, with customer-managed KMS in Private/Dedicated, Redwood does not persist plaintext keys. The runtime requests cryptographic operations from the KMS in your account. There is a small caveat for some managed hosted variants where transient plaintext exists in memory during processing; we're happy to document our memory handling and controls for the SIG.
[03:49] Rajiv: Ok we need that in writing — memory handling, who has root, etc. Also pen test and vulnerability management evidence.
[03:56] Samir: We can provide a redacted penetration test summary and our vuln management policy. Claire, do we have the last pentest date?
[04:04] Claire: Last external pentest was 2026-02-15; redacted summary is available. We run quarterly internal scans and track remediation in JIRA.
[04:12] Laura: For procurement we typically need this attached to the SIG.
[04:15] Samir: Noted, we'll attach the pentest summary to the SIG answer as evidence.
[04:20] [04:20] — brief crosstalk —
[04:25] Claire: Moving on to data residency: hosted Redwood default region is us-east-1 and eu-west-1. For Dedicated we can pin to a region and for Private we can deploy in your VPC/your data center. Tempest's note on the form said all customer data must remain in EU region for certain products.
[04:40] Marcus: Correct — retail product data must stay within EU. Can you confirm Dedicated in eu-west-1 satisfies that?
[04:46] Claire: Yes, Dedicated pinned to eu-west-1 keeps processing and storage in that region. We can provide deployment topology diagrams showing network boundaries.
[04:55] Rajiv: Also network segmentation and VPC peering — do you support PrivateLink or dedicated transit?
[05:01] Claire: We support AWS PrivateLink for hosted endpoints and VPC peering for Dedicated. For Private we set up customer-defined subnets and routing. We'll include network diagrams.
[05:11] Samir: We'll add architecture diagrams to the artifact links.
[05:14] Laura: On the SIG there's a question about incident response — expected notification windows and post-incident evidence.
[05:22] Claire: Our standard is 72-hour notification for confirmed incidents that impact confidentiality, integrity or availability. For Dedicated/Private customers we offer accelerated SLAs and a named contacts channel. We can provide an incident response playbook and historical post-incident reports redacted.
[05:36] Rajiv: Will that be in the procurement contract or is it an add-on?
[05:40] Samir: Incident SLAs are part of enterprise agreements for Dedicated customers; hosted customers have the standard terms. We'll note it in the SIG response and you can flag if you need contractual language.
[05:51] Marcus: A couple of technical clarifications — does Redwood store KV cache or embeddings separately? We want to make sure embeddings derived from customer content are deleted on request.
[06:01] Claire: We have explicit controls: embeddings and derived artifacts are stored per-tenant and can be configured with retention policies. For Hosted we default to 90 days for ephemeral caches but embeddings can be retained longer if the customer opts in. We support deletion APIs and will furnish proofs of deletion where required.
[06:18] Rajiv: Proofs of deletion — like an S3 lifecycle or deletion log?
[06:22] Claire: Deletion logs and event records with timestamp and actor are available; we'll show an example event record (redacted) as evidence.
[06:29] Laura: On the SIG there's a question about third-party sub processors. Who are your main sub processors?
[06:35] Samir: Primary cloud providers — AWS and GCP for regions, Datadog for observability, and a few managed infra partners. We list full sub processor list in the DPA.
[06:44] Rajiv: We need to see the DPA and the subprocessors list.
[06:48] Samir: We'll attach the DPA and the current subprocessor list.
[06:51] Claire: Quick note on audit: customers can request on-site audits for Dedicated/Private deployments under the enterprise agreement; hosted audits are limited to SOC reports and third-party attestations.
[07:03] Marcus: For encryption in transit — TLS versions and cipher suites?
[07:07] Claire: We use TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers (we'll include the exact cipher list in the SIG answer). Mutual TLS is available for some private endpoints.
[07:16] Rajiv: Good. Also there's a SIG control about separation of duties and privileged access — who has admin keys and how is that logged?
[07:24] Claire: Privileged access is limited to a small group, RBAC enforced, and all access is logged in the audit trail. We use MFA, JIT access with time-limited sessions, and require approval for any root-level operations. We'll provide our privileged access matrix as redacted evidence.
[07:39] Samir: I'll flag that in the SIG answers.
[07:42] Laura: A procurement-specific question — pricing for Dedicated with 12-month log retention and CMK is needed.
[07:48] Samir: For Dedicated with 12-month retention and CMK, we'll put together a quote; it's typically a capacity plus add-on for extended log retention and KMS connector. I'll follow up with a formal quote in the next 48 hours.
[07:59] Rajiv: One more: regulatory attestations for payments — do you have any PCI reachability?
[08:04] Claire: We do not hold PCI certification; we can sign a scope-limiting DSA and deploy Private so payment card data never touches Redwood. We can also work with your teams on tokenization strategies.
[08:18] Marcus: Sounds good.
[08:20] [08:20] — slight overlap, some filler words —
[08:25] Samir: Ok to recap quickly: we'll send the completed SIG spreadsheet with answers and attached evidence (SOC 2, pen test summary, DPA/subprocessor list), Claire will add SSO/SCIM examples and KMS notes, and we'll follow up on quote for Dedicated + retention + CMK. Customer to confirm a time for technical deep-dive with Marcus.
[08:45] Laura: That works. Please include the specific contact for your security lead too.
[08:50] Samir: Will do, I'll include security@redwood.example.com and our Head of Security (Elena Morales) as the contact.
[08:58] Rajiv: Thanks, also can you call out where you have "shared responsibility" versus customer controls — that's important for our audit team.
[09:06] Claire: Absolutely, every SIG answer will have a control owner column — Redwood or Customer — and we'll mark the evidence.
[09:13] Marcus: For the deep-dive, we want to focus on KMS flow and network topology; can Claire run that?
[09:19] Claire: Yes, happy to. Proposed slot week of 2026-07-27.
[09:24] Samir: I'll propose times after this call.
[09:27] Laura: One last procurement nit — we may ask for a limited liability carve-out for security incidents, but that's later in the legal review.
[09:33] Samir: Understood.
[09:35] Rajiv: That's all from me. Thanks everyone.
[09:38] Samir: Thanks all, we'll send the artifacts and follow up.
[09:41] Claire: Bye.
[09:42] Laura: Bye.
[09:43] Marcus: Bye.
